purpose: Reading platter for foundational architectural treatises — the proportion, order, and modular-composition systems (Palladio's orders, Durand's grid method) indexed for citation in AC papers.
posture: Index and citation only. PDFs are fetched into sources/ (gitignored) by fetch-sources.mjs from their public hosts (Internet Archive, Getty Virtual Library); nothing is mirrored into the repo. The Getty Durand translation is in copyright and distributed free by Getty — cite it, never redistribute it.

checked_key.true: citation details confirmed against a primary or publisher source during a platter pass
checked_key.false: written from working knowledge; wants a verification pass before it is cited in a paper

shelves.treatise: Primary treatises — the books themselves, in their canonical scanned or publisher editions.

sources.title: The Four Books of Architecture
sources.venue: London: Printed for R. Ware (Isaac Ware's English edition of I quattro libri dell'architettura, Venice 1570)
sources.why: The canonical proportional system: the five orders (Book I), villa plans (Book II), civic works (Book III), Roman temples (Book IV). Getty Research Institute scan of Ware's 1738 folio — the plate-accurate English edition. The locator marks the spread this ingestion started from.

sources.title: Précis of the Lectures on Architecture; with, Graphic Portion of the Lectures on Architecture
sources.venue: Los Angeles: Getty Research Institute, Texts & Documents series. Introduction by Antoine Picon; translation by David Britt. Original: Précis des leçons d'architecture données à l'École polytechnique (Paris, 1802–1805) + Partie graphique (1821)
sources.why: The proto-computational treatise: Durand replaces Vitruvian proportion with a modular grid, combinatorial composition of standard elements, and economy as the governing criterion — architecture as a generative procedure. The most direct historical ancestor of piece-based composition.
